title: How to Read the Newcastle and Hunter Commercial Property Market
excerpt: A practical framework for testing current commercial property evidence before making a location or lease decision.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Newcastle and Hunter Commercial Property Guide | YOS
metaDescription: Learn how to assess current Newcastle and Hunter commercial property evidence before making a lease decision.
body:
Commercial property conditions change by precinct, building, use and timing. A useful market view should be based on current evidence for the exact requirement, not a broad headline.

## Define the requirement first

Record the preferred locations, area range, use, timing, services, access, parking and fitout needs. This determines which properties and transactions are genuinely comparable.

## Separate asking evidence from transaction evidence

Listings show availability and landlord expectations. They do not, on their own, prove the final commercial terms agreed. Label each source clearly.

## Compare like with like

Building quality, floor efficiency, condition, accessibility, services and lease structure can explain large differences. Avoid combining unlike properties into one benchmark.

## Date every observation

Availability, incentives and competing demand can change. Record when information was collected and verify it again before relying on it.

## Test the complete proposal

Compare total occupancy cost, operational suitability, fitout implications, timing and lease risk. Independent legal, financial, planning and technical advice may also be required.

Your Office Space can prepare a current evidence pack for a defined Newcastle or Hunter requirement and coordinate the commercial comparison.
